question: Why do we actually study nursing theories in school? What is their main job?

options.A: To dictate how much medication a patient should receive
options.B: To eliminate the need for doctor and nurse collaboration
options.C: To guide clinical practice and provide a scientific base
options.D: To replace hospital policies and procedure manuals

explanation: Think of nursing theories as the bedrock of our profession! They give us a clear, scientific reason for the way we care for patients every single day. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h1)

question: Patient, health, environment, and nursing. Why are these four big ideas so special in our field?

options.A: They represent the four core pillars that define nursing practice
options.B: They are required elements for hospital budget planning
options.C: They determine the legal penalties for medical malpractice
options.D: They outline the exact daily schedule for ward nurses

explanation: Spot on! These four concepts make up the 'metaparadigm' of nursing—basically, the big four pillars that every single nursing theory builds upon. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h1)

question: If Florence Nightingale could whisper advice to you on the ward today, what would she say is the true focus of nursing?

options.B: Manipulating the patient's environment to promote healing

explanation: You got it! Nightingale was all about fresh air, clean water, and bright light. She believed in setting up the environment so the patient's body could heal itself. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h2)

question: You walk into a stuffy ward, fling the windows open to let in fresh air, and tidy up a messy bedside. Whose classic nursing theory are you putting into action?
explanation: Brilliant! Opening windows and clearing away dirt are the ultimate trademark moves of Nightingale's Environmental Theory. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h2)

question: Virginia Henderson is famous for giving us a clear checklist of fundamental human needs. How many are there on her list?
explanation: It's 14! Henderson outlined fourteen basic human needs that help us figure out exactly what kind of care our patients require. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h3)

question: A stroke patient is too weak to hold a spoon or brush their teeth. According to Virginia Henderson, what should you, the nurse, do?

options.A: To prescribe nutritional supplements for faster recovery
options.B: To discharge the patient immediately to family members
options.C: To assist the patient with activities they cannot currently do alone
options.D: To wait until the patient regains full strength without helping

explanation: Spot on! Henderson taught us that the nurse's role is to step in and act as hands or strength for the patient when they can't quite manage on their own yet. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h3)

question: In Dorothea Orem's theory, what exactly does a 'self-care deficit' mean?

options.A: The hospital has run out of supplies needed for patient hygiene
options.B: The doctor has forbidden the patient from eating solid foods
options.C: The patient's need for self-care is greater than their ability to do it
options.D: The nurse refuses to help the patient walk around the ward

explanation: You nailed it. A self-care deficit simply happens when the care a person needs is higher than what they are currently able to pull off by themselves. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h4)

question: Your patient knows how to inject their own insulin, but they need you to teach them how to calculate food portions. Which of Orem's systems is this?
explanation: Well done! In a supportive-educative system, the patient can do most things themselves, but they still need guidance, teaching, and support from you. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why is knowing your nursing theories so helpful when working in a busy, resource-strapped Nigerian hospital?

options.A: It ensures that doctors no longer have to visit the patient wards
options.B: It prevents patients from ever being admitted to public hospitals
options.C: It eliminates the need for any medical supplies in the hospital
options.D: It helps nurses prioritize care and maintain standards despite challenges

explanation: Exactly! When resources are tight, nursing frameworks keep our focus sharp on what matters most: patient safety and essential human needs. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h5)

question: There is a sudden water shortage at the clinic, so you quickly improvise a clean handwashing station before dressing a wound. What are you doing here?

options.A: Practicing a fully compensatory self-care deficit model
options.B: Ignoring standard nursing care procedures entirely
options.C: Failing to follow strict hospital administration rules
options.D: Controlling the environment to prevent infection

explanation: Brilliant improvising! Finding a way to maintain cleanliness even when infrastructure fails is the true spirit of environmental control and safe nursing. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h5)
